summary: A Kootenai National Forest lookout near Libby, begun about 1930 per a newspaper and dated 1934 by firelookout.com; abandoned 1942 and gone.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a pole observation tower; a 1930 newspaper item says the tower was to be 85 ft
facts.status_note: firelookout.com: Abandoned 1942. Gone. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list reads Tower Gone. Forest Lookouts shows no status.

events.note: July 1930 Western News item (quoted by Forest Lookouts): a new lookout station under construction on Big Hoodoo with an 85-ft tower; Jack Halfstead to be stationed there. Conflicts with firelookout.com's 1934 date.
firelookout.com dates the L-4 cab and pole observation tower to 1934.
September 1938 Montana Standard item (quoted by Forest Lookouts): CCC youths were ordered to a farm by a Hoodoo mountain forest lookout. No observer named.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. firelookout.com gives 1934; the July 1930 Western News item, quoted by Forest Lookouts, describes a station under construction that year. The story reports both dates. The sources do not say whether the 1930 plan and the 1934 structure are the same tower.

notes_for_editor: Gone status is consistent across firelookout.com (Abandoned 1942. Gone.) and the FFLA list (Tower Gone); the Forest Lookouts entry has no status line. Build date conflict: a July 1930 newspaper item (via Forest Lookouts) describes construction and an 85-ft tower; firelookout.com dates the L-4 cab to 1934. Height 25.9 m comes from the 1930 newspaper figure, not a later source. Staffing evidence: a July 1930 item says Jack Halfstead was to be stationed there, and a single 1938 item mentions a Hoodoo lookout without naming an observer. Elevation 5,236 ft from firelookout.com; the record has no elevation field. Record fields agree (county Lincoln, agency Kootenai NF). Did not check the 1930 Western News or the 1938 Montana Standard originals, or NHLR and Forest Service records; one web search found nothing more specific. Site today and access are unknown.
